title: Windows MSYS2 host-Python and ONNX Runtime bootstrap hotfix
line_endings: CRLF, as checked out on Windows. `sha256` in each entry is over the exact bytes shipped, so APPLY_HOTFIX.ps1's post-copy verification is byte-for-byte.

defects_fixed.symptom: PATH `python` resolved to C:\msys64\mingw64\bin\python.exe, which reports os.name == 'nt' and then creates a POSIX-scheme .venv/bin/python.exe on Windows
defects_fixed.fix: explicit host-interpreter classification decided by the venv scripts scheme, plus an automatic fallback to a supported standard Windows CPython found through the Python Launcher

defects_fixed.symptom: pip reported no matching distribution for onnxruntime==1.24.0 after resolving torch
defects_fixed.fix: pinned to 1.24.1, the smallest published patch in the same release family, verified against the package index and measured bit-identical to the historical runtime on the frozen SCRFD detector

defects_fixed.symptom: latent, found by auditing the plan rather than by failing: the cu129 index publishes torch 2.13.0 for Linux only, and --extra-index-url would have let pip install a different build from PyPI while the manifest went on naming the CUDA index it never used
defects_fixed.fix: the host wheel platform is now a selection gate checked before compute capability; every profile declares the platforms its index actually publishes; a Windows Blackwell host resolves to the new cuda-cu130 profile; and the installed torch build is read back and refused if it does not carry the selected profile's CUDA tag

defects_fixed.symptom: the failed install left a .venv that existed, ran and was missing packages
defects_fixed.fix: the environment is classified and repaired: dependencies are installed into a structurally sound .venv, and only an unusable one is rebuilt. No manual deletion.

not_shipped.why_not_shipped: the GPU laptop runs the pipeline, not the suite; ship it only if you intend to run pytest there
